audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers currently read Ryze / Skill / Yone / Yone / Ryze / Yone / Yone, which contradicts the already-audited Ryze-side chart.
audit.why: mirrorFindings point 2 records the opposite direction as Yone, Yone, Skill, Yone, Ryze, Ryze, Yone. The two directions must state the same facts, and mirror-fix.js would overwrite any disagreement introduced here. The mirror reading is also defensible from the kit: level 1-2 belong to a mobile Yone against an immobile 615-range Ryze, level 3 is even as Rune Prison and Overload come online, and Ryze's 6 and first-item windows are real (see point 3).
audit.corrected: Set both layers to Yone, Yone, Skill, Yone, Ryze, Ryze, Yone and re-point the whys at the same reading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says 'Level 6 favors you since Realm Warp adds nothing in a duel', treating Ryze's 6 as a non-spike.
audit.why: Realm Warp has a passive half that the page never mentions: 'Passively, Overload deals even more damage against targets with Flux.' Ryze gains combat power at 6 without casting the ultimate at all. His first mana item then scales Arcane Mastery, which adds damage to every spell based on bonus mana. Those are the two windows where Ryze is genuinely ahead.
audit.corrected: Name the Realm Warp passive as the level-6 spike and the first mana item as the follow-up, instead of writing 6 off as free for Yone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound (E) is described twice as an 'untargetable' window used to dodge Overload.
audit.why: Riot's E text grants Move Speed and a forced snap-back that repeats a portion of the spirit damage. There is no untargetability in the text and no such flag on the ability. A player told E dodges Overload will eat the Q into Rune Prison root that the page itself calls Ryze's one kill combo. Note also that Overload and Spell Flux carry the projectile flag, but Yone has no projectile-blocking tool, so that is not writable.
audit.corrected: Rewrite E as a move-speed gap-close whose snap-back repeats part of the damage, and keep the actual dodge instruction on Rune Prison (11/10.5/10/9.5/9s), which is the cooldown that decides the lane.

audit.why: Rune Prison at 11s rank 1 is correctly identified as the punishable cooldown, and Spell Flux at 3.5s is too short to play around — the page does not try to, which is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Rune Prison only roots when Flux is already on the target — otherwise it is a slow.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' That makes Spell Flux the tell, not Rune Prison itself: if he has not landed E, his W cannot lock you down.
audit.corrected: Watch for Spell Flux landing first — a Rune Prison with no Flux on you is only a slow, and that is a free window to commit.

notes: The packet defect flagged wants.you[1] 'Use Soul Unbound' as a probable wrong name — that is a FALSE POSITIVE, Soul Unbound is the correct Riot name for Yone's E. The genuine error in that same string is mechanical, not nominal: it claims E dodges Overload via untargetability, which Riot's text does not grant. Chart follows the already-written Ryze-side audit (mirrorFindings point 2) rather than packet.levelChart, which reads Yone on all seven rows and disagrees with the mirror at rows 5 and 6. Ratings adjusted alongside the flipped rows; the mirror's exact rating values were not recorded in mirrorFindings, so if the Ryze side used different numbers, mirror-fix will reconcile.
